Structural Conservation. Its purpose is not to make energy constant, but to discourage sudden jumps that destabilize training. A useful implementation keeps the core small enough to inspect during experiments. The practical consequence is straightforward. Its purpose is not to make energy constant, but to discourage sudden jumps that destabilize training. The baseline should remain small enough for fast experiments and clear enough for later extensions.

Structural Conservation. The best baseline reports conservation next to language loss so failures are visible early. If conservation spikes repeatedly, the run should be inspected for an excessive learning rate or drift scale. If conservation remains small while prediction loss decreases, the structural path is behaving well. A careful baseline keeps this mechanism visible. The update rule combines a batch summary with the previous core state, then applies bounded drift. The baseline should remain small enough for fast experiments and clear enough for later extensions.

Memory Compression. The memory path should remain auxiliary, because the backbone must still learn ordinary sequence patterns. Attention compression lets the model read relevant summaries without replaying the entire buffer. This keeps memory bounded even when the training run lasts for many thousands of steps. A good memory experiment compares generation quality with memory enabled and disabled. This matters during long training runs. The attractor is learned, so it can adapt to the corpus while still discouraging runaway motion. This section treats the mechanism as an engineering constraint rather than a metaphor.
